paragraphs.text: Julius Caesar was born here in 100 BCE at an approximate location.
In 88 BCE the consul Sulla led the March on Rome, the first time a general ordered his army to march against the Republic; its placement is approximate.
In 82 BCE Sulla won the Battle of the Colline Gate at the northeastern end of Rome and secured control of Italy.
Augustus, also known as Octavian, was born here in 63 BCE; this placement is approximate.
On the Ides of March, 44 BCE, a group of senators assassinated Julius Caesar during a Senate session at the Curia of Pompey in Rome, stabbing him approximately 23 times.
Tiberius was born in Rome in 42 BCE at an approximate location.
From 41 BCE to 40 BCE the Perusine War, a civil war placed only approximately here, was fought by Lucius Antonius in support of Mark Antony against Octavian.
In 49 CE the emperor Claudius expelled Jews from Rome; this placement is approximate.
The Great Fire of Rome began in July 64 CE around the Circus Maximus, and nearly three quarters of Rome was destroyed.
In 69 CE, the Year of the Four Emperors, Galba, Otho, Vitellius, and Vespasian ruled in succession amid turmoil in Rome and the provinces.
That year also brought the Siege of the Capitoline Hill and a Battle of Rome, the latter at an approximate location.
Construction of the Colosseum began under the Emperor Vespasian and was completed under his successor Titus.
